default_value.description: Use a value, or a fallback when it is empty, like a first name or "there" when a contact has none. Zero and false count as values.
default_value.display_str_template: Use {0}, or {1} if it is empty
default_value.name: default_value

parameters.description: The value to use when it isn't empty.
parameters.name: value

parameters.description: What to use instead when the value is missing, blank, or an empty list.
parameters.name: default

returns.description: The value, or the fallback when the value is empty.

encode_text.description: Make text safe to put in a web address, HTML, JSON, Markdown or a Slack message, encode or decode Base64, or remove accents and emoji.
encode_text.name: encode_text

parameters.description: The text to encode or decode.
parameters.name: text

parameters.description: How to change the text.
parameters.name: encoding

options.label: Safe for a web address (a b → a%20b)
Back from a web address (a%20b → a b)
Plain letters, no accents or emoji

returns.description: The text, encoded or decoded.

endswith.description: Check whether text ends with specific words or characters.
endswith.name: endswith

parameters.description: The text to check.
parameters.name: text

parameters.description: The text it should end with, such as .pdf.
parameters.name: suffix

parameters.description: Match upper- and lower-case letters exactly (the default). Turn this off to treat them as the same.
parameters.name: case_sensitive

returns.description: Whether the text ends with the text given.

extract.description: Pull matches out of text: an email address, web address, phone number, domain, number, or your own pattern.
extract.name: extract

parameters.description: The text to search, such as the body of an email.
parameters.name: text

parameters.description: What to pull out of the text.
parameters.name: type

parameters.description: A regular expression to search for. Used only when Extract is set to Custom pattern.
parameters.name: pattern

parameters.description: Return only the first match, or every match as a list.
parameters.name: all_matches

parameters.description: The country of phone numbers written without a country code. Defaults to the United States.
parameters.name: region

returns.description: The first match, or a list of every match when all matches are asked for. Numbers come back as numbers, and finding nothing gives empty text, or an empty list.

format_phone.description: Write a phone number one standard way, however it was typed, like +1 415-555-0123 or +14155550123 for a texting app.
format_phone.name: format_phone

parameters.description: The phone number, written any way.
parameters.name: text

parameters.description: How to write the number.
parameters.name: style

parameters.description: The country of numbers written without a country code. A number that starts with its own, like +44, is read in that country instead. Defaults to the United States.
parameters.name: region

returns.description: The phone number, written the chosen way.

format_text.description: Change the letter case of text: make it uppercase, lowercase, capitalize the first letter, use title or sentence case, or turn it into a slug for a web address.
format_text.name: format_text

parameters.description: The text to change the letter case of.
parameters.name: text

parameters.description: How the text should be cased.
parameters.name: case

returns.description: The text in the chosen letter case.

html_to_markdown.description: Turn HTML, like an email's body or a web page, into Markdown that reads as plain text and keeps its headings, lists, links, bold and italic, tables and code: ready for an AI step, a Slack message or a note. Scripts and styles are left out.
html_to_markdown.name: html_to_markdown

parameters.description: The HTML to convert, a whole page or a piece of one.
parameters.name: text

returns.description: The Markdown.

join.description: Turn a list into one piece of text.
join.name: join

parameters.description: The list of values to combine into one piece of text.
parameters.name: items

parameters.description: Use empty text to join with nothing.
parameters.name: separator

returns.description: The list's items as one piece of text, with the separator between each.

json_query.description: Pick out part of some data, or of JSON text, with a JMESPath query, like the ids of every open item: items[?status=='open'].id.
json_query.name: json_query

parameters.description: The data to search, such as an API's response, or JSON written as text.
parameters.name: value

parameters.description: A JMESPath query (jmespath.org), like orders[0].email for the first order's email, or items[?price > `100`].name for the names of items over 100.
parameters.name: query

returns.description: What the query picked out; blank when it found nothing.

json_to_xml.description: Turn data or JSON text into an XML document, for an API or a service that speaks XML, a feed or a file: each field becomes an element named after it, a list repeats its element, and a field named like @id becomes an attribute.
json_to_xml.name: json_to_xml

parameters.description: The data to write as XML: a record or a list from an earlier step, or JSON text.
parameters.name: data

parameters.description: The name of the element that wraps everything, like order or request. Defaults to root.
parameters.name: root

returns.description: The XML document, indented, with an XML declaration on its first line.

lookup.description: Turn one value into another with a small table you fill in, like US to United States or a status code to a label, instead of a chain of If steps.
lookup.display_name: Look up a value in a table
lookup.name: lookup

parameters.description: The value to find in the table, like a country code.
parameters.name: value

parameters.description: Each value to look for, and what to give back for it. Letter case and spaces around a value don't matter.
parameters.name: table

parameters.description: What to give back when the value isn't in the table. Leave empty to get a blank.
parameters.name: fallback

parameters.description: Match upper- and lower-case letters exactly. Off by default, so us, US and Us all match.
parameters.name: case_sensitive

returns.description: What the table gives for the value, the fallback when it isn't there, or a blank without one.

make_csv.description: Write rows as CSV text, to put in a message or send to an API. A list of records gets a header row of their fields. To attach a CSV file, use Create a file instead.
make_csv.name: make_csv

parameters.description: The rows to write, such as the rows a sheet returned or a list of records.
parameters.name: rows

parameters.description: What goes between the columns.
parameters.name: separator

returns.description: The rows as CSV text, header row first.

markdown_to_html.description: Turn Markdown, like an AI step's answer or a template you write, into plain HTML for a web page, a rich-text field or an app that takes HTML: headings, lists, links, bold and italic, tables and code all come through. For an email, use HTML's Turn text into HTML, which adds the styles email apps show.
markdown_to_html.name: markdown_to_html

parameters.description: The Markdown to convert. A line break in it is a line break in the HTML, and HTML tags in it pass through.
parameters.name: text

returns.description: The HTML, without <html> or <body> around it and with no styles, ready to put in a page or a field.

match_keywords.description: Score text against your keyword lists to see how well it matches. Useful for tagging, filtering, or deciding what should happen next.
match_keywords.name: match_keywords

parameters.description: The text to score. Letter case is ignored.
parameters.name: text

parameters.description: Most important words or phrases. Each match adds 3 points.
parameters.name: strong_terms

parameters.description: Fairly important words or phrases. Each match adds 2 points.
parameters.name: medium_terms

parameters.description: Minor words or phrases. Each match adds 1 point.
parameters.name: weak_terms

parameters.description: Total points needed to count as a match. Defaults to 3.
parameters.name: threshold

returns.description: Whether the text matched, its score, and which keywords it contains.

is_match.description: Whether the score reached the score needed.

matched_terms.description: The keywords found, strong ones first, each with the list it came from.

score.description: 3 points for each strong keyword found, 2 for each medium one, and 1 for each weak one.

pad_text.description: Make text a set length by adding a character to its start or end, like 42 written as 0042 for an invoice number. Text that is already that long stays as it is.
pad_text.name: pad_text

parameters.description: The text or number to pad, like 42.
parameters.name: text

parameters.description: How many characters long it should be, like 4.
parameters.name: length

parameters.description: The character to add. Defaults to 0.
parameters.name: character

parameters.description: Which end of the text to add the characters to.
parameters.name: side

returns.description: The text, padded to the length.

parse_csv.description: Turn CSV written as text, such as an export pasted into an email or returned by an API, into rows keyed by the header row, the way Read a file reads a CSV file.
parse_csv.name: parse_csv

parameters.description: The CSV, header row first.
parameters.name: text

parameters.description: What separates the columns. Work it out reads the text and picks the one that fits.
parameters.name: separator

parameters.description: Whether the first row names the columns. Without one, columns are column_1, column_2 and so on.
parameters.name: has_header

returns.description: The rows, keyed by the header row.

rows.description: One record per row, keyed by column name.

parse_json.description: Turn JSON written as text, like an AI step's answer or a webhook body, into data whose fields later steps can use.
parse_json.name: parse_json

parameters.description: The text holding the JSON. It may be wrapped in a code block or a sentence.
parameters.name: text

returns.description: The data the JSON holds, usually a record or a list.

plain_text.description: Turn HTML, like an email body or a web page, or Markdown into plain text for a sheet, a text message or a plain email: tags and formatting marks removed, paragraphs, line breaks and bullets kept, and each link's address shown after its text.
plain_text.name: plain_text

parameters.description: The HTML or Markdown to turn into plain text.
parameters.name: text

parameters.description: What the text is written in.
parameters.name: source

options.label: HTML (an email body, a web page)

returns.description: The text as a person reads it, without markup.

replace.description: Find text and replace it with something else.
replace.name: replace

parameters.description: The text to search through.
parameters.name: text

parameters.description: The text to find, or a pattern. Every occurrence is replaced.
parameters.name: search

parameters.description: The text to put in its place.
parameters.name: replace

parameters.description: Match upper- and lower-case letters exactly (the default). Turn this off to treat them as the same.
parameters.name: case_sensitive

parameters.description: The exact text, or a pattern (a regular expression). With a pattern, $1 in the replacement puts back what its first group in brackets matched, $2 the second.
parameters.name: search_type

returns.description: The text with every occurrence of the text searched for replaced.

split.description: Split text into a list. Spaces around each piece are left out.
split.name: split

parameters.description: The text to break into pieces.
parameters.name: text

parameters.description: The text to break at, such as a comma or a space.
parameters.name: delimiter

returns.description: The pieces of the text between the separators.

starts_with.description: Check whether text starts with specific words or characters.
starts_with.name: starts_with

parameters.description: The text to check.
parameters.name: text

parameters.description: The text it should start with.
parameters.name: prefix

parameters.description: Match upper- and lower-case letters exactly (the default). Turn this off to treat them as the same.
parameters.name: case_sensitive

returns.description: Whether the text starts with the text given.

text_contains.description: Check whether text includes specific words or characters.
text_contains.name: text_contains

parameters.description: The text to search through.
parameters.name: text

parameters.description: The exact text to look for.
parameters.name: substring

parameters.description: Match upper- and lower-case letters exactly (the default). Turn this off to treat them as the same.
parameters.name: case_sensitive

returns.description: Whether the text includes the text searched for.

text_length.description: Count how many characters are in text.
text_length.name: text_length

parameters.description: The text to measure.
parameters.name: text

returns.description: The number of characters in the text.

text_part.description: Take a piece of text: what comes before or after a word or character, what sits between two, or a number of characters from a position. For example, the name before the @ in an email address.
text_part.name: text_part

parameters.description: The text to take a part of.
parameters.name: text

parameters.description: Which part of the text to take.
parameters.name: part

parameters.description: The word or characters to look for, like @ or Order #. Letter case doesn't matter, and the first one found is used.
parameters.name: marker

parameters.description: Where the part ends: the next time this appears after the text looked for.
parameters.name: end_marker

parameters.description: The first character to take: 1 is the first character, -1 the last, -4 the fourth from the end.
parameters.name: start

parameters.description: How many characters to take. Leave empty for the rest.
parameters.name: count

returns.description: The part of the text, without spaces around it. Blank text when what was looked for isn't there.

trim.description: Remove spaces, tabs, and line breaks from the start and end of text.
trim.name: trim

parameters.description: The text to trim.
parameters.name: text

parameters.description: Which ends to trim: both ends, only the start, or only the end. Defaults to both ends.
parameters.name: mode

returns.description: The text with spaces, tabs and line breaks removed from its start, its end, or both.

truncate.description: Shorten text so it fits within a set number of characters. By default no ending is added; set an ending like “…” to append one when text is cut. The ending counts toward the limit, so the result never exceeds it.
truncate.name: truncate

parameters.description: The text to shorten.
parameters.name: text

parameters.description: Text longer than this is shortened.
parameters.name: length

parameters.description: Optional ending added when text is shortened, e.g. “…”, counted within the character limit. Leave blank (the default) to shorten without any ending.
parameters.name: ellipsis

parameters.description: Keep whole words instead of cutting one in the middle. When on, the text is shortened at a word boundary, so the result may come out a little shorter than the limit.
parameters.name: dont_split_words

returns.description: The text cut to at most the given number of characters, the ending included, or unchanged if it was short enough.

validate_text.description: Check whether text is a valid email address, web address, phone number, number or domain name, or whether it matches a pattern of your own.
validate_text.name: validate_text

parameters.description: The text to check, such as an email address, web address or phone number.
parameters.name: text

parameters.description: What kind of value to check for.
parameters.name: type

parameters.description: The country of numbers written without a country code. A number that starts with its own, like +44, is checked against that country instead. Defaults to the United States.
parameters.name: region

parameters.description: A regular expression the text must contain a match of, like ^INV-\d{4}$ for an invoice number. Start it with ^ and end it with $ to test the whole text.
parameters.name: pattern

returns.description: Whether the text is a valid email address, web address, phone number, number or domain name, or matches the pattern, whichever was chosen.

word_count.description: Count how many words are in text.
word_count.name: word_count

parameters.description: The text whose words are counted.
parameters.name: text

returns.description: The number of words in the text.

xml_to_json.description: Turn XML, like an API's response or a feed, into data whose fields later steps can use, the way Read a file reads an XML file: each element is a field named by its tag, a tag that repeats is a list, and attributes are fields too.
xml_to_json.name: xml_to_json

parameters.description: The XML to convert.
parameters.name: text

returns.description: What the outermost element holds: a record of its elements and attributes, or its text when it holds only text. Text stays text, so a number in the XML is text like "3".

yes_no.description: Turn a value like Yes, TRUE, 1, on, a ticked box or No into a real true or false, for a checkbox field or an API that needs one.
yes_no.name: yes_no

parameters.description: The value to read as yes or no, like a sheet's checkbox or a form's answer.
parameters.name: value

parameters.description: What to make of text that is neither a yes nor a no, like Pending. Blank is always no.
parameters.name: otherwise

returns.description: True for a yes, false for a no.
